The '''1964 Danish 1st Division''' ([[Danish language|Danish]]: '''Danmarksturneringens 1. division 1964''') was the 37th season of Denmark's top-flight association football division since the establishment of Danmarksturneringen's [[Danish football league system|nation-wide league structure]] in 1927, and the 51st edition of the overall [[List of Danish football champions|Danish national football championship]] since its inception in 1912. Governed by the [[Danish Football Association|Danish FA]], the season was launched on 26 March 1964 with a clash between last season's third-placed [[Boldklubben 1903|B 1903]] and [[Østerbro]]-based and local rivals [[Boldklubben af 1893|B.93]] with the last round of six matches concluding on 15 November 1964.<ref name="has-1d1964" /> [[Esbjerg fB]] were the defending league champions, having won their third consecutive league title [[1963 Danish 1st Division|last season]], while [[Boldklubben Frem|BK Frem]] and [[Boldklubben af 1893|B.93]] entered as promoted teams from the [[1963 Danish 2nd Division]]. Fixtures for the 1964 season were announced by the Danish FA's tournament committee on 6 January 1964, featuring a nine weeks long summer break.<ref name="dfo-07.01.1964" />

The club leading the league table after the spring season's first eleven matches were awarded a berth to the [[1964–65 European Cup#Preliminary round|1964–65 European Cup preliminary round]], while the winners of the [[1963–64 Danish Cup]] would quality for the first round of the [[1964–65 European Cup Winners' Cup]] — in case, it turned out to be the same team, the runners-up of the [[1964 Danish Cup Final]] would instead quality for the European Cup Winners' Cup tournament. The overall league winners of 1964 qualified for the [[1965–66 European Cup#Preliminary round|1965–66 European Cup preliminary round]].<ref name="pedfod" /> The Danish representatives in the [[1964–65 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup#First round|1964–65 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup first round]] became [[Boldklubben 1913|B 1913]] (on behalf of [[Odense-Stævnet]]) and [[Kjøbenhavns Boldklub|Kjøbenhavns BK]] (on behalf of [[Stævnet]]).<ref name="akt-08.06.1964" /><ref name="akt-26.06.1964" />

[[Boldklubben 1909|B 1909]] won the league, secured their second [[List of Danish football champions|Danish league championship]] on the final matchday in front of a record high attendance of 43,400 spectators at [[Københavns Idrætspark]], the highest at a Danish league match in history, with [[Aarhus Gymnastikforening|Aarhus GF]] becoming the runners-up for the fourth time in the history.<ref name="df-dt1964" /><ref name="ber-storm" /> At the end of the season, the two clubs with the fewest points in the final league standings, [[Akademisk Boldklub|Akademisk BK]] and [[Brønshøj Boldklub|Brønshøj BK]], were relegated to the [[1965 Danish 2nd Division]].<ref name="df-dt1964" /> [[Jørgen Ravn]] of [[Kjøbenhavns Boldklub|Kjøbenhavns BK]] was the league's top scorer for the second time, scoring 21 goals, three more than second-placed teammate [[Finn Møller]].<ref name="guinness90" /><ref name="rsssf-1d1964" />

==Summary==
{{external media
| float  = right
| image1 = [https://web.archive.org/web/20200414170042/https://filweb.arkibas.dk/filer/visning/f32c0599ed63a001dcf52a08c7969ef3 The players of B 1909 at the award ceremony], crowned 1964 [[List of Danish football champions|Danish league champions]], following the away match against [[Kjøbenhavns Boldklub|Kjøbenhavns BK]] on 15 November 1964. [[Bruno Eliasen]] is holding the league trophy.
}}

The 1964 top-flight league was inaugurated early with a single Thursday match between [[Boldklubben 1903|B 1903]], that had finished the 1963 season in third place, and newly promoted [[Boldklubben af 1893|B.93]] at [[Gentofte Stadium]] on 26 March 1964 in front of an audience of 3,100 spectators.<ref name="bt-28.03.1964" /><ref name="has-1d1964" /> B.93's [[Svend Petersen (footballer)|Svend Petersen]] scored the season's first goal after 8 minutes of play via a header, following a pass from forward Walther Jensen and left wing Tom Søndergaard, but B 1903's knee-injured defender Henning Westergaard managed to draw the match 1–1 by netting in the second goal of the game in the 89th minute after B.93's goalkeeper Bent Jørgensen had lost the ball.<ref name="bt-28.03.1964" />

B 1909 claimed the league title on the final matchday, 15 November, with a 1–0 away win at [[Københavns Idrætspark]] in a top flight clash against another title contender [[Kjøbenhavns Boldklub|Kjøbenhavns BK]].<ref name="ber-storm" /> The weather on that Sunday was cold, windy and raining, but the deciding match of season managed to attract a crowd of 43,400 spectators — it remains the official standing record attendance for a Danish league game.<ref name="ber-storm" /><ref name="dbuk-ki" /> Before the last round, both teams were leading the league table, each with 29 points, followed by Aarhus GF in third place with 27 points — B 1909 held a slightly better [[goal average]].<ref name="has-1d1964" /> The interest for the game was fueled by the fact that the past [[List of Danish football champions|ten top-tier league seasons]] had been won by provincial teams, and that the game involved a [[Copenhagen]]-based team, which could reclaim the Danish league title — the first 41 editions of Danish national football championship had been won by a club from the capital.<ref name="ber-storm" /> Despite the stadium being able to hold approximately 50,000 spectators at the time and no brewing unrest, the authorities decided the close the gates 15 minutes before [[Kick-off (association football)|kick-off]] due to fears of overcrowding.<ref name="ber-storm" /> A good portion of non-payers had more or less illegally obtained a spot at the stands inside the stadium, while several thousand people outside the stadium could not get access.<ref name="ber-storm" /><ref name="b09-h3d" />

The final match was won by B 1909 with a single goal netted by forward [[Mogens Haastrup]] in the 80th minute of play, following a pass from teammate [[John Danielsen]], where Haastrup dribbled and eluded Kjøbenhavns BK goalkeeper Nils Jensen.<ref name="b09-h3d" /> B 1909 goalkeeper [[Svend Aage Rask]], dressed in complete black, prevented several goal attempt from Kjøbenhavns BK's forwards, including [[Jørgen Ravn]].<ref name="b09-h3d" /> [[Hungarians|Hungarian]]-[[Swiss people|Swiss]] [[Carlos Pintér]] was head coach for the [[Odense]]-based [[working class]] team in corporation with a match selection committee and had the following core players in the club's squad: goalkeeper [[Svend Aage Rask]], defenders [[Leif Hartwig]] and [[Jørgen Rask]], midfielders [[Arno Hansen]], [[Erling Nielsen (footballer)|Erling Nielsen]] and Per Jacobsen, and forwards [[Palle Kähler]], [[Walther Richter]], Mogens Haastrup, John Danielsen and [[Mogens Berg]].<ref name="b09-h3d" /> Palle Hansen, Mogens Engstrøm and [[Bruno Eliasen]], who all appeared in the last game of the season, including Jørgen Petersen and Poul Erik Wiinberg, also played their part in the winning season.<ref name="b09-h3d" /><ref name="fh-b09" /><ref name="b09-mh" />

[[Boldklubben Frem|BK Frem]] and [[Boldklubben 1903|B 1903]] secured themselves another season in the top-flight division by winning their last games on 15 November 1964, 4–0 at home against [[Vejle Boldklub|Vejle BK]] and 3–1 away against [[Nykøbing Falster Boldklub af 1901|B 1901]], respectively.<ref name="bkf-s1964" /><ref name="frem125" /><ref name="has-1d1964" /> The decisive match for BK Frem took place at [[Valby Idrætspark]] in front of an audience of 3,000 spectators compared to the club's other home matches in the season, that had all been played at Københavns Idrætspark.<ref name="bkf-s1964" /><ref name="frem125" /> [[Akademisk Boldklub|Akademisk BK]], who was also part of the relegation battle, won their last match away against [[Boldklubben 1913|B 1913]], but ended up with just one point short in the final standings, so was relegated to the [[1965 Danish 2nd Division]] along with [[Brønshøj Boldklub|Brønshøj BK]].<ref name="has-1d1964" />

==Teams==
<!--{{See also |List of Danmarksturneringen clubs}}-->
Twelve teams competed in the league – the top ten teams from the [[1963 Danish 1st Division|previous season]] and the two teams promoted from the [[1963 Danish 2nd Division|second-tier]]. The promoted teams were [[Boldklubben af 1893|B.93]], returning to the top flight after a four-year absence, and [[Boldklubben Frem|BK Frem]], returning after a three-year absence. They replaced [[Aalborg Boldspilklub|Aalborg BK]] and [[Køge Boldklub|Køge BK]], ending their top flight spells of one and three years respectively.

==League table==
Every team played two games against the other teams, at home and away, totaling 22 games each. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal average]]. The team with the most points were crowned winners of the league, while the two teams with the fewest points would be relegated to the [[1965 Danish 2nd Division]].
